## Document Overview {#sec-overview}

This Access Control Policy establishes the requirements to ensure the protection of
{{< var environment_name >}}s within the scope of the {{< var organisation >}} Research Data
{{< var isms_abbr >}} by managing access rights. This policy supports compliance with ISO 27001,
ensuring that access to information is based on business needs and aligned with security
requirements.

<!-- isms:end id=overview.intro -->

<!-- isms:override id=user-access.approval-chain mode=replace
     reason="Oxford names three approvers with different scope and wording from the
     baseline's generic approval-chain hint: Information Asset Owner/Administrator per study,
     Environment Owner for infrastructure and non-human accounts, and Supporting Service
     Owner for IT services."
     approved-by="Sarah Waters" approved-date=2026-09-11 -->

- New users or a change to user access shall be approved by:
  - The {{< var roles.asset_owner >}} or an {{< var roles.asset_administrator >}} (for a study): for
    information assets stored within a {{< var environment_name >}} project.
  - {{< var roles.environment_owner >}}: for user access to infrastructure and code managing a
    {{< var environment_name >}}, including non-human (service accounts).
  - {{< var roles.service_owner >}} or their delegate: for access to any supporting IT service.

<!-- isms:end id=user-access.approval-chain -->

## Privileged Access Management {#sec-privileged-access}

Administrative or privileged accounts shall be tightly controlled and limited to authorized
personnel. Privileged accounts should only be used for administrative activities. Privileged access
management shall be controlled through a formal process and only the minimum privileges will be
granted to carry out the role or task. A formal record of all privileges allocated will be
maintained.

<!-- isms:end id=privileged-access -->

<!-- isms:override id=physical-access mode=replace
     reason="Oxford names the Service Owner of a facility (not the baseline's generic

     generic 'approved personnel'."
     approved-by="Sarah Waters" approved-date=2026-09-11 -->

## Physical Access {#sec-physical-access}

Physical access shall only be granted on the authority of the Service Owner of a facility. All
physical information systems shall be protected in accordance with their value and classification
according to the Information Classification Policy. Approved Researchers shall be responsible for
physical security measures in offices and other shared spaces to prevent unauthorised access to data
via an end point device as detailed in the Approved Researcher Agreement.

<!-- isms:end id=physical-access -->

<!-- isms:override id=network-access mode=replace
     reason="Oxford states Network Access as prose rather than the baseline's bulleted list,
     and phrases segregation as a 'should' recommendation determined by risk assessment
     results rather than the baseline's 'shall'."
     approved-by="Sarah Waters" approved-date=2026-09-11 -->

## Network Access {#sec-network-access}

Diagnostic and configuration ports shall only be enabled for specified business reasons. All unused
ports shall be disabled or removed. Changes to network configuration affecting
{{< var environment_name >}} networks will be risk assessed and recorded. Segregation of networks
should be implemented as determined by the results of the risk assessment.

<!-- isms:end id=network-access -->

<!-- isms:override id=os-access mode=replace
     reason="Oxford's Operating System Access bullets differ in wording throughout (each
     starts 'All users shall be required to...') and name the University of Oxford Password
     Policy explicitly."
     approved-by="Sarah Waters" approved-date=2026-09-11 -->

## Operating System Access {#sec-os-access}

- All users shall be required to confirm they are an authorised user at log-on.
- All users shall be required to change their passwords periodically and in accordance with the
  {{< var organisation >}} Password Policy.
- All user sessions shall be configured to lock automatically after a period of inactivity in order
  to reduce the risk of unauthorised access.
- Where technically possible, all standard accounts that are delivered with operating systems shall
  be disabled, deleted or have their "default" passwords changed on system installation.

<!-- isms:end id=os-access -->

<!-- isms:override id=information-system-access mode=replace
     reason="Oxford phrases the first two bullets differently and moves the Environment
     Owners' segregation duty out of the bulleted list into a trailing paragraph."
     approved-by="Sarah Waters" approved-date=2026-09-11 -->

## Information System Access {#sec-information-system-access}

- Where adequate assurance is absent, account access shall be disabled such that re-enablement shall
  only follow evidence of adequate assurance.
- Removal of accounts shall also include the removal of any associated access rights.

{{< var roles.environment_owner >}}s shall group together information assets as appropriate to
achieve the required segregation on networks.

<!-- isms:end id=information-system-access -->

<!-- isms:override id=monitoring mode=replace
     reason="Oxford's Monitoring and Logging paragraph differs in wording throughout (log
     field list, 'anomalous activity', and conditional reporting on a judgement that
     unauthorised access occurred) and drops the baseline's reference to organisation-specific
     incident management procedures."
     approved-by="Sarah Waters" approved-date=2026-09-11 -->

## Monitoring and Logging {#sec-monitoring}

Access to {{< var environment_name >}}s shall be logged and monitored for the purpose of
investigating security incidents. Logs should include 'date/time/name/reason' and should be reviewed
periodically to detect any unauthorised access attempts. Anomalous activity or violations shall be
assessed and, where unauthorised access is judged to have occurred, will be reported as an
information security incident.

<!-- isms:end id=monitoring -->
